intro: Read a job advert and learn the vocabulary of applications, working conditions and employment.
p.oferta de trabajo.consejo: A company publishes it when it looks for someone. You say «buscar una oferta» and «responder a una oferta».
p.currículum.consejo: It comes from Latin and has an accent. You also say «currículo» or, short, «CV».
p.entrevista.consejo: You say «tener una entrevista» or «acudir a una entrevista». It is pronounced with «b»: en-tre-BIS-ta.
p.contrato.consejo: You sign a contract with «firmar». It can be «de un año» or «indefinido», with no end date.
p.sueldo.consejo: The ue sounds «we»: SWEL-do. «Salario» means almost the same and is widely used.
p.experiencia.consejo: The x sounds «ks»: eks-pe-RYEN-thya. Here it is an uncountable noun: «tengo experiencia».
p.ascenso.consejo: You get an ascenso with «conseguir». The verb is «ascender»: «la han ascendido a jefa».
p.despedir.consejo: It changes e to i: «despido», «despide», but «despedimos». With «se», «despedirse» is to say goodbye.
p.dimitir.consejo: Whoever «dimite» leaves by choice; whoever is «despedido» is dismissed.
p.autónomo.consejo: For a woman it is «autónoma». You say «ser autónomo» or «trabajar de autónomo».
p.informe.consejo: It is a document, not a person who informs. In the office you «preparar» or «entregar» an informe.
p.formación.consejo: It ends in -ción, so it has an accent on the o and is feminine: «la formación».
p.candidato.consejo: For a woman it is «candidata». It is the person who applies for an advert.
b1.titulo: How to read a job advert
b1.texto:
Many adverts use **se** so they do not name the company: **se busca una persona**, **se buscan dos personas**. The verb agrees with what comes next: **se requiere experiencia**, **se requieren dos años de experiencia**.

A vacancy may ask for **experiencia**, **formación**, languages or **disponibilidad**, and offer a **contrato**, a **sueldo**, **horario flexible** or the chance of **ascenso**.

To get the job: **enviar el currículum**, **acudir a una entrevista** and, if they choose you, **firmar el contrato**. Later they may **despedirte**, or you may **dimitir** or **jubilarte**.

A worker can be **empleado**, **autónomo** (self-employed), **funcionario** (in public administration) or **estudiante en prácticas**.
b2.f0.texto: Look at this job advert from a transport company.
b2.f2.texto: Experience and a good level of English are required.
b2.f4.texto: They offer a one-year contract and training at the company.
b2.f5.texto: There is also a chance of promotion.
b2.f7.texto: If they call me, I will be one of the candidates.
b4.texto:
In adverts, **se** + verb hides who is speaking. The verb agrees with the noun that follows:

- **Se busca** una persona (singular).
- **Se buscan** dos personas (plural).

If you talk about someone you do not know yet, after **quien** or **para quien** comes the subjunctive: **Hay ascenso para quien demuestre interés**.

Watch **despedir**: it changes e to i in **despido**, **despides**, **despide**, **despiden**, but not in **despedimos**.
b4.e0.texto: A person with experience is wanted.
b4.e1.texto: Two people with experience are wanted.
b4.e2.texto: There is promotion for whoever shows interest.
b5.f0.texto: The office corridor smells of new carpet and freshly made coffee.
b5.f1.texto: Six candidates wait seated on grey chairs next to a plant.
b5.f2.texto: All of them carry a CV in a cardboard folder.
b5.f3.texto: A young woman quietly goes over her answers about the salary.
b5.f4.texto: An older man looks at the wall clock and breathes slowly.
b5.f5.texto: Suddenly a door of light wood opens.
b5.f6.texto: A woman with glasses says the name of the first candidate.
b5.f7.texto: The young man stands up, smooths his jacket and walks in with a firm step.
b5.f8.texto: The door closes without a sound behind him.
b5.f9.texto: In the corridor everyone watches the closed door with a mixture of fear and hope.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! The verb agrees with «años», which is plural.
b6.o1.refuerzo: It is singular, but «dos años» is plural.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The infinitive does not work: a conjugated verb is needed here.
b7.o1.refuerzo: That is it! An «autónomo» works for himself, with no boss.
b7.o2.refuerzo: A «candidato» is still applying for the job.
b7.pregunta: What do you call someone who works for himself?
b8.frase: Se ofrece un contrato de un año
b9.o0.refuerzo: Well done! «Despedir» is to dismiss someone from their job.
b9.o1.refuerzo: A promotion is moving up; it is the opposite of a dismissal.
b9.o2.refuerzo: A contract is signed when you start, not when you are dismissed.
b9.pregunta: The company «despide» an employee. What happens?
b10.o0.refuerzo: «Demuestra» is the ordinary present: it works for a person you already know.
b10.o1.refuerzo: The infinitive does not work: a conjugated verb is needed.
b10.o2.refuerzo: That is it! If the person is unknown, the subjunctive is used.
b10.pregunta: Which form follows «quien» if you do not know the person?
b12.o0.refuerzo: The interview is a conversation to get the job.
b12.o1.refuerzo: A promotion is a step up; you do not get it every month.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Yes! The salary is the money you get every month.
b12.pregunta: What do you get every month for your work?
b13.frase: Marta decidió ____ porque quería cambiar de trabajo.
b13.o0.refuerzo: The company «despide»; Marta leaves because she wants to.
b13.o1.refuerzo: Well done! «Dimitir» is leaving your post by your own choice.
b13.o2.refuerzo: «Ascender» is moving up, not changing jobs.
b13.pregunta: Which verb fits someone who leaves their post?
p.transportes.consejo: Plural of «transporte». «Empresa de transportes» is a transport company.
p.piden.consejo: The e becomes i in «pido, pides, piden», but not in «pedimos».
p.requiere.consejo: In adverts, «se requiere» + noun means it is needed.
p.ofrecen.consejo: The «c» sounds like «th» before e: o-FRE-then.
p.posibilidad.consejo: Words ending in -dad are feminine and stressed on the last syllable.
p.envía.consejo: Command for «tú». The accent on í keeps i and a in separate syllables.
p.llaman.consejo: The «ll» sounds like y. «Me llaman» can mean they call me.
p.seré.consejo: Future of «ser». The accent marks the stress on the last syllable.
p.candidatos.consejo: Plural of «candidato». For a mixed group, use the masculine.
p.buscan.consejo: In adverts, «se buscan» + plural noun: «se buscan dos personas».
p.demuestre.consejo: Subjunctive of «demostrar». It goes after «quien» for an unknown person.
p.interés.consejo: The accent keeps the stress on the last syllable. Plural: «intereses».
p.moqueta.consejo: Said in Spain for a carpet fixed over the whole floor.
p.sentados.consejo: Participle of «sentarse». It agrees with the people: «sentados».
p.planta.consejo: It is also a floor of a building: «la planta baja» is the ground floor.
p.respuestas.consejo: Plural of «respuesta». It comes from the verb «responder».
p.miran.consejo: «Mirar» is to look with attention. «Ver» is just to see.
p.esperanza.consejo: It comes from «esperar». The «z» sounds like «th»: es-pe-RAN-tha.
p.requieren.consejo: Plural of «se requiere»: «se requieren dos años». The e becomes ie.
p.pierde.consejo: The e becomes ie: «pierdo, pierde», but «perdemos».
p.decidió.consejo: Past (indefinido) of «decidir». The accent marks the final stress.
p.marta.consejo: A name, so it is written with a capital letter.
